name: amigit
readme:
Short:        Local-only git CLI for AmigaOS 3.x (preview)
Type:         dev/misc
Architecture: m68k-amigaos >= 68020
Uploader:     duncan@bowring.us
Author:       Duncan Bowring (amiport, built on libgit2)
Version:      0.1-4
URL:          https://github.com/bdgscotland/amiport

amigit 0.1-4 -- DEVELOPER PREVIEW

This is an early developer preview, NOT a stable git client.
Suitable for early testers and feedback. Not yet suitable for
managing real projects.

What works today:
  - Local repository operations: status, log, show, diff, add,
    commit, branch, checkout, tag
  - Reading existing repos created by another git
  - Single-letter assigned-volume init (T:foo, R:foo after
    AmigaDOS Assign)

What does NOT work yet:
  - amigit init from a multi-character volume name (WORK:,
    Ram Disk:, System 3.1:). You have to AmigaDOS Assign a
    single-letter alias first. See 'Init friction' below.
  - Network: no clone, no fetch, no push, no remote, no pull.
    The whole collaboration value of git is missing. amigit
    currently only manages LOCAL repositories.
  - Multi-line commit messages via -m. Use a single shell token
    for now; -F <file> is planned.
  - Merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, stash. None implemented.
  - Color output, pager integration, interactive flows.

The init friction:
  Out of the box, 'amigit init' from a typical Shell prompt
  (1.WORK:>, 1.Ram Disk:>) does NOT work. The libgit2 library
  this port embeds only recognizes single-character drive
  prefixes (X:) as path roots. AmigaOS multi-character volume
  names confuse it. amigit detects the case at startup and
  emits a friendly error pointing at the workaround.

  Workaround:
    1.WORK:> Assign R: WORK:
    1.WORK:> R:
    1.R:> amigit init R:myproject

  We are working on a real fix. See PORT.md inside the LHA for
  the engineering notes on three approaches that were tried in
  the 0.1.x line and rolled back.

Roadmap:
  0.2 -- init works from any volume + cheap perf wins. Removes
        the friction wall above. Target: weeks, not months.
  0.3 -- bundled libgit2 / zlib rebuilt at -m68020 for real
        perf gain on accelerated Amigas (Vampire / 030 / 040).
  1.0 -- HTTPS clone, fetch, log, diff against public repos
        via a libgit2 smart-HTTP backend on AmiSSL. Target:
        roughly 6-10 weeks of focused work. This is the
        watershed release -- the moment amigit becomes a tool
        you would actually use to explore real codebases on
        AmigaOS.
  Future -- HTTPS push, libssh2 SSH support, merge / rebase /
           stash. Probably another 4-8 weeks beyond 1.0.

What this preview is good for:
  - Validating the libgit2 + amiport posix-shim stack on real
    AmigaOS hardware (your A2000+Vampire, A1200, A3000 / 4000)
  - Walking the history of an existing .git/ directory copied
    over from a Linux machine
  - Experimenting with a journal-style local-only workflow
  - Reporting bugs that help shape 0.2 / 0.3 / 1.0

What this preview is NOT good for:
  - Daily git workflow on real projects (yet)
  - Collaboration via GitHub / GitLab / etc (no networking yet)
  - Anything that requires merge, rebase, or stash

Project: https://github.com/bdgscotland/amiport
Built on: libgit2 1.8.5, zlib 1.3.1, amiport posix-shim

Cross-compiled with m68k-amigaos-gcc 6.5.0b for AmigaOS 3.x.
Targets 68020 minimum. Tested in FS-UAE A1200 with 82/82
functional tests passing -- but those tests cover synthetic
happy paths and do not yet exercise the full real-world
workflow. Real workflow validation is a 0.2 milestone.

Binary: ~1.05 MB. Stack: 256 KB. Requires 4 MB free RAM at
runtime.
porting_notes: DEVELOPER PREVIEW (0.1.x line). First git client implementation effort for AmigaOS 3.x. Written from scratch as an amiport-native CLI on top of the pruned lib/libgit2/libgit2.a (1.8.5) because upstream git's fork()/execvp()-based command dispatch is structurally infeasible on 68k AmigaOS. 0.1-4 is a metadata-and-copy reframe that flips the public maturity tag from 'stable' to 'preview' and rewrites the readme to be honest about what works and what doesn't. The 0.1.x line is a proof-of-concept that proves libgit2 can be embedded into a 68k binary and that the on-disk git format works under libnix file I/O -- it is NOT yet a usable git client for daily work. Three honest gaps: (1) 'amigit init' from a typical Shell prompt on a multi-char volume name doesn't work without an AmigaDOS Assign workaround (libgit2 git_fs_path_root limitation, three real-fix attempts tried and rolled back -- see PORT.md), (2) no networking yet (clone/fetch/push need a custom libgit2 smart-HTTP backend on AmiSSL, ~6-10 weeks of focused work tracked as the 1.0 milestone), (3) the 82-test suite covers synthetic happy paths rather than real-world workflows -- the user's first attempt hit the init wall in minute one. Roadmap: 0.2 = init works from any volume + cheap perf wins; 0.3 = libgit2/zlib rebuilt at -m68020 for real perf; 1.0 = HTTPS clone/fetch/log against public repos. Bug reports welcome.
known_limitations: DEVELOPER PREVIEW -- not yet stable for daily use. (1) No network commands at all -- clone/fetch/push/pull/remote/submodule require bsdsocket + libssh2 or http-shim in a future Phase 4 (1.0 milestone). The collaboration value of git is missing. (2) 'amigit init' from a multi-character volume name ('WORK:', 'Ram Disk:', 'System 3.1:') produces a friendly error pointing at the AmigaDOS Assign workaround -- libgit2's git_fs_path_root only recognizes single-character ASCII drive prefixes. Workaround: 'Assign R: WORK: ; amigit init R:foo'. Real fix deferred. (3) The 82-test suite covers synthetic happy paths; full real-world workflow validation is a 0.2 milestone. (4) No merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, or stash. (5) No interactive flows (rebase -i, add -i, commit --amend with editor). (6) Commit messages via -m must be single shell tokens (-F <file> planned). (7) No color output, no pager integration. (8) Empty initial commits rejected. (9) Requires 4 MB free RAM at runtime. (10) 68020 minimum -- no plain 68000/A500 support.
